Session 04 · M03 · Conditional risk, expected value & simulation

Make decisions under uncertainty

Distinguish joint from conditional probability, compare payoffs across states, and inspect risk alongside averages.

Case: CloudFlowBadge: Risk navigator

Before class

Readiness check

Three questions, one minute. Your score suggests a path through the lesson.

Take the check
1. For P(event | positive screen), what is the denominator?

That denominator belongs to sensitivity, P(positive | event).

Correct. Conditioning on a positive screen restricts the reference group.

The whole population is used for a joint proportion, not this conditional probability.

2. Does higher expected profit guarantee higher profit next time?

Expected value averages across states. One realized state can be worse.

Correct. Check downside, assumptions, and decision horizon as well.

Display size does not change uncertainty.

3. What does the fifth percentile of profit mean?

Some outcomes are worse. It is not a floor.

Correct. Describe the model and horizon as well as the percentile.

A percentile describes position, not the mean.
